status_at_declaration: prospective; not executed; frozen by build_package.py

questions.H8: Products: on the RTX 4090, is the signed multiply-add butterfly variant (modal8_muladd) faster than the fastest FP64 donor kernel (fused_ai_fp64, fused_fp64, node_fp64) and than modal8, at identical inputs?
questions.H9: Inside multigrid-preconditioned CG (all-FP64, identical outer iterations), is mg64-modal8_muladd faster than the fastest FP64 donor arm and than mg64-modal8?
questions.H10: Under an FP32 V-cycle inside FP64 CG, what is the outer-kernel effect of modal8_muladd, and which route is fastest to a 1e-8 true residual?
questions.R: Replication: do H8-H10 hold on a second, different RTX 4090 host (different provider machine id) running the byte-identical package?

solver.outer: flexible CG (Polak-Ribiere), FP64, true-residual test every iteration with residual replacement

multigrid.omega: 4/(3 lambda_l), lambda_l by 30 seeded power iterations on the FP64 hierarchy with node_fp64 finest; shared by all arms
multigrid.coarse_levels_kernel: node_fp64 (FP64 arms) / node_fp32 (FP32 V-cycle arms), identical for all arms
multigrid.coarsest_solve: dense Cholesky of the constrained operator assembled on the host, shared by all arms

fixed_work.rule: K = max converged outer iterations of mg64-fused_ai over its to-tolerance repetitions; every arm runs exactly K outer iterations

h8.rule: H8 passes on a host iff, on both primary cases, the paired per-round product ratio (fastest donor by median / modal8_muladd) has median >= 1.05 and one-sided 95% bootstrap lower bound >= 1.02, all rounds present and all product checks passed. The ratios vs modal8, modal8_signbit and dense8 are reported descriptively.

h9.rule: H9 passes on a host iff, on both primary cases, the fixed-work paired ratio (fastest FP64 donor arm / mg64-modal8_muladd) has median >= 1.05 and lower bound >= 1.02 with identical work in every fixed-work solve and a completed run.

h10.rule: descriptive: fastest arm that physically passes all repetitions per case; outer-kernel effect = fixed-work paired ratio of mg32-fused_ai64-node32 over mg32-modal8_muladd-node32.

replication.rule: A claim is stated as replicated only if it passes on both hosts. A host whose run fails or is incomplete counts as not replicated, never as excluded. The second host must have a different provider machine_id from the first.

not_claimed: novelty of the parity decomposition, of the signed multiply-add butterfly (Dao AI Lab) or of geometric multigrid
cpu_preflight: CPU dry run of the whole schedule with NumPy products (reduced hierarchy) before declaration; bitwise identity of the three butterflies checked on a NumPy emulation corpus (tests).

provenance.kernel_variants: modal8_muladd and modal8_signbit differ from the measured Voxel modal8 kernel only in the butterfly expression (dependencies/cuda.py _VARIANT_BUTTERFLY); JPDC sections 63, 77-79, 88 measured the same butterflies in a different (halo) layout.
provenance.attribution: modal8_muladd is an FP64 adaptation of the Dao AI Lab fast-hadamard-transform warp butterfly (commit e7706faf8d1c3b9f241e36860640ad1dac644ede, BSD-3-Clause); see dependencies/ATTRIBUTION.md and DAO-LICENSE.
provenance.expectation_before_data: JPDC section 88 (RTX 4090, halo layout): signed_muladd 1.85-2.15x over its dense control; Voxel sessions A/D: modal8 1.22-1.26x (products) and 1.14x (mg64 fixed work) over fused_ai. Not a prediction threshold; the decision rules below are.

products.vector: seeded standard normal (order_seed + q), constrained DOFs zeroed; raw operator product timed
